title: The golangci-lint step adds a bogus tool line, and the build then fails
foundBy: deps-maintenance campaign, pilots 1 and 2: the pilot2 orchestrator's findings (campaign-workspaces/deps-maintenance/pilot2/archives/deps-pilot2-20260922T203209Z/orchestrator/output/findings.md) and the step corrections pilot3's coordination.md section 5 carries
details:
A `routine:go` action emits `go get -modfile=go.golangci.mod -tool github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2@v2.13.2`. The `-tool` flag names the module root rather than its command. Run as printed in a clone of ledger's main of 2026-09-22, it adds `github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2` to the tool block beside the real `.../v2/cmd/golangci-lint`, and prints `cannot find module providing package`. The pilots saw the linter's build then fail on a missing `go.sum` entry.

`golang.org/x/tools` has the same fault the other way round. It is an indirect requirement in `go.golangci.mod` and the module of the `deadcode` tool in `go.mod`, and the action emits `go get -modfile=go.golangci.mod -tool golang.org/x/tools@v0.50.0`: a second bogus tool line, and `go.mod` never moves. `go mod tidy -modfile=go.golangci.mod`, the obvious repair, is wrong as well. Run on ledger's main of 2026-09-22, it adds 59 lines to `go.golangci.sum` and a requirement on ledger itself. Tidy reads the packages in the directory rather than the tool the file exists for.
